Why are air and water called nature's treasures?
questions.a: No life can survive without them - they are free gifts of nature we must keep clean.

questions.q: How does air help living things?
questions.a: It gives oxygen to breathe, CO2 to plants, and carries sounds and weather.

questions.q: Name two ways water is used besides drinking.
questions.a: Cooking, washing, farming (irrigation) and generating electricity.

questions.q: Why are forests called the green treasury?
questions.a: They give timber, fruits, medicines and hold soil and water for all.

questions.q: Name three things humans take from forests.
questions.a: Wood, honey and medicinal plants (also gum, fodder).
They give food, shelter (homes) and safe breeding places.
Rocks are hard natural masses of minerals; soil is the loose upper layer where plants grow.

Why should we use fossil fuels carefully?
questions.a: They formed over millions of years, cannot be replaced, and burning them pollutes.
